ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A is directly above point O, and there is a pulley at A; one end of the light rod OP is hinged at point O, and the other end is point P. Rod OP is inclined in the vertical plane, and the angle between OP and the vertical direction is marked as α. A heavy object G is hung downward from end P; there is also a light rope from point P connected to the pulley at A, then passing around the pulley and being acted on by pulling force F toward the lower left. Reasoning: Take point P as the object of study. Point P is acted on by three forces: the vertically downward pulling force G of the heavy object on it; the tension T of the rope along the PA direction; the elastic force N of the light rod OP on point P along the rod direction. Let OP=l, OA=h, AP=s. Take O as the origin and the vertical upward direction as the y-axis, then the coordinates of point P relative to point O can be written as (l sinα, l cosα), and the coordinates of point A are (0,h), so the direction vector from P pointing to A is (-l sinα, h-l cosα), and its length is s. Equilibrium in the horizontal direction: N sinα = T·l sinα/s, therefore N = T·l/s. Equilibrium in the vertical direction: N cosα + T(h-l cosα)/s = G. From the horizontal-direction equation, T/s = N/l. Substitute into the vertical-direction equation: N cosα + (N/l)(h-l cosα)=G, that is, N cosα + Nh/l - N cosα = G, so Nh/l=G, obtaining N=Gl/h. Since G, l, and h are all constants, N is unrelated to α. Therefore, when α slowly decreases, the magnitude of the elastic force of rod OP remains unchanged.
